title: The remote viewing photo protocol and its 35% hit rate, replicated at Edinburgh and the Rhine institute
place_text: SRI; University of Edinburgh; Rhine Research Institute, Duke, North Carolina

tellings.quote: the study of these attempts found that there was an overall hit rate of 35% a number that was found to be repeatable over and over again

plain: In remote viewing tests, where a person tries to describe a hidden photograph using the mind alone, a study of the attempts is said to have found an overall hit rate of 35 percent, a number that came up again and again. Michels tells this himself on an episode with a guest named Eric Wargo, citing a researcher named Jessica Utts and saying the result was repeated at the Stanford Research Institute, the University of Edinburgh and the Rhine Research Institute in North Carolina. If true, it would mean the mind can gather information beyond the ordinary senses.
